title: Judge a report against the checkpoint of the turn that produced it
prompt:
Read, in crates/spawn-core/src/bridge.rs, `advance()`, `follow_output()`, `checkpoint()` and the fold that sets `Active::checkpoint` from an event's `checkpoint_reason()`; in crates/spawn-core/src/observe/classify.rs, `live_execution()` (when a session is `TurnStoppedIdle`) and in observer.rs when an observation is written; `collect_reports()` in crates/spawn-cli/src/deliver.rs and `Facts::turn_stopped_idle` in dispatch.rs; `spawn_task_reported` in crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql; `freshness()`, `pushed_candidate()` and `judge_pushed()` in crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs; and docs/storage.md (checkpoints, the pusher, landing).

The problem. A worker's report is collected, and the task judged, before the checkpoint of the turn that wrote the work exists. Two paths lead there:
- The Bridge records a turn's end (`turn.stopped`) in one tick but takes that turn's checkpoint in the next. It sets `Active::checkpoint` only when it folds the event it read back from the log. In between, the Observer and the dispatcher run (`spawn loop`: Bridge tick, Observer tick, dispatcher step), so the report is collected while the agent's latest `artifact.committed` is an older one, or there is none at all.
- The Observer calls a session `TurnStoppedIdle` on a ready screen alone (`screen == Ready`), so a report can be collected before the transcript's end of the turn has even been read.
The integrator then judges the agent's pushed branch against whatever checkpoint exists. With no checkpoint and a pushed branch, `freshness()` says `Fresh`. The branch pushed when the workspace was mounted is the task's base, so real work is rejected with "the work changes nothing on main", sent back to the worker, and counted toward the mission's halt (three in a row). It happened live: task 24 on mission 6 was rejected exactly that way. (There the branch really lacked main's commit, but the verdict path is the same.) Objective 009's scenario had to work around it by reporting only after its checkpoint was pushed.

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks). The property is at the source: a report is judged against the checkpoint of the turn that produced it.
1. A turn's checkpoint is part of the turn's end. No report is collected before the turn that wrote it has ended in the log (the transcript's end of the turn, not only a ready screen) and that turn's checkpoint has been taken. That includes a turn whose checkpoint changes nothing (no new commit, so no `artifact.committed`): its checkpoint is the branch head as it stands, and its report must still be collected. One way that holds wherever the Observer and dispatcher run: when the Bridge reads a turn's end from the transcript, it commits the workspace and records `artifact.committed` first, then records `turn.stopped`. The dispatcher then collects a report only once the session's latest turn event in the log is a turn's end (`turn.stopped` or `turn.failed`), not a newer `message.received`.
2. The `task.reported` control record names that checkpoint: `"commit": <id>`, the agent's checkpoint the report's turn ended with. It is an `artifact.committed` of the agent recorded before the report, and its tree holds what the turn wrote. It is null only when the agent has no checkpoint at all. Add a `spawn_task_reported(bigint, text, text)` for it, and keep `spawn_task_reported(bigint, text)` working with a null commit: rsi/scenarios 004, 007 and 008 call it, and so do the tests in crates/spawn-postgres/tests/control.rs.
3. The integrator judges a reported task against its report's commit. The pushed head must be that commit or a descendant of it (and of the agent's latest checkpoint, as now). Otherwise the verdict is `stale`, as today: no gate run, no rejection counted, nothing sent to the worker. A task whose report names a commit is never judged `Fresh` for lack of a checkpoint. A report with a null commit (records from before this change) is judged as today.
4. A trap. An Observer with no model judge writes a new judgement only when its verdict changes. A fact recorded after the idle judgement (the turn's end, read after the screen showed the prompt, or anything else the turn records) makes `Facts::current_observation()` empty, and the worker sits idle with nobody judging it again. Rule 1 must not turn that into a report that is never collected. The log's own end of the turn is newer evidence than the judgement, and may be what the collection rests on, as long as the worker is live, has no command open, and its latest judgement is `TurnStoppedIdle`.
State the rule in docs/storage.md (checkpoints and landing) and in the module comments of deliver.rs and integrate.rs. Add unit tests:
- in the Bridge: a turn's end recorded after its checkpoint, and an unchanged turn;
- in deliver.rs: no report collected on a ready screen before the turn's end, and a report collected after it with the commit;
- in integrate.rs: freshness with a report's commit (equal, descendant, behind, no pushed branch).

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/010.sh (read it). A real `spawn loop` (no model judge, no supervisor) runs ephemeral workers of a gated mission (accept = gate) with a fake engine. `spawn integrate --once` passes, run as soon as a task is reported, judge them with a recording gate (SPAWN_GATE) that accepts every candidate. A `git` first in PATH makes every checkpoint commit (`commit-tree` with a "spawn checkpoint ..." message) take 4 s longer.
- (1) One turn writes the work and the report, as a real engine does.
- (2) One turn writes the work. Once its checkpoint is pushed, a second turn writes only the report, and that turn's checkpoint changes nothing.
For each task: it lands within 150 s with no `rejected` verdict, the mission's gate_rejections stay 0 and it never halts, and main holds the file. Its `task.reported` record's `commit` is a checkpoint of the agent recorded before the report, whose tree holds the file; in (2), the first turn's checkpoint. On 693c46e it fails at (1) with "the work changes nothing on main". It exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails, 2 on a harness failure.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, rename, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation ([lints] tables, clippy.toml, a new crate-level #![allow]/#![expect], a removed #![warn]/#![deny]) and any build-time code (build.rs, .cargo/, a `build =` key in a Cargo.toml). The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
